# PlanMyProject - Copilot & Codex Instructions

These instructions are specific to this repository. Follow them for any task related to build, test, versioning, packaging, release notes, or Marketplace publishing.

## Scope

- Extension: `Plan My Project`
- Package name: `plan-my-project`
- Publisher: `aypande`
- Manifest: `package.json`
- Extension entrypoint: `main: ./out/extension.js` (a single esbuild bundle)

## Repository Truths (Do Not Assume Generic Templates)

- Source lives in `src/`, organized by subsystem (`controller`, `model`, `parser`, `queue`, `scanner`, `ai`, `generation`, `research`, `debate`, `ui`, `storage`, `util`).
- `out/extension.js` is produced by `esbuild.js` (bundle, `vscode` external). `tsc` is used only for type-checking (`--noEmit`) and for the test build. Never expect per-file output in `out/`.
- Tests live in `test/*.test.ts` and `test/integration/*.test.ts`, compiled by `tsconfig.test.json` into `out-test/`. Benchmarks live in `test/bench/*.bench.ts` and are **not** part of `npm test`.
- Test runtime is Node's built-in test runner (`node --test`) with `NODE_PATH=./test/shims`. The scripts use explicit directory globs, not `**`, because the CI Node version cannot expand globs for `node --test`. **A new test directory needs a `package.json` script change** or it will silently never run.
- `FEATURE_CHECKLIST.json` lists features with the test file and literal test name that proves each one; `npm run check:coverage` verifies them. A template-literal test name must appear in the checklist as the literal, unexpanded `${...}` source text.
- Every setting in `contributes.configuration` must declare an explicit `scope`; `npm run check:settings-scope` enforces it.
- Build status in `README.md` is auto-generated by `scripts/update-readme-build-status.js` (it runs `tsc --noEmit`, the tests and coverage).
- `vscode:prepublish` is `npm run compile && npm run build`, so `vsce package` and `vsce publish` both recompile and rewrite the README build-status block.
- Packaging/publishing is done with `@vscode/vsce` via npm scripts.
- This repo does not define a lint script. Do not invent one.

## Canonical npm Scripts

Always use these scripts from `package.json` unless the user explicitly asks otherwise:

```bash
npm run compile              # rimraf out + tsc --noEmit + esbuild bundle -> out/extension.js
npm test                     # test:build + node --test (unit + integration)
npm run bench                # benchmark suite with committed baselines (test/bench/baseline.json)
npm run check:coverage       # FEATURE_CHECKLIST.json entries all backed by real tests
npm run check:settings-scope # every setting declares a valid scope
npm run test:coverage        # tests with --experimental-test-coverage
npm run build                # README build-status refresh (tsc + tests + coverage)
npm run package              # npx @vscode/vsce package --no-yarn --no-dependencies
npm run publish:vsce         # npx @vscode/vsce publish --no-yarn --no-dependencies
```

## Hard Guardrails

1. Never publish if `npm run compile`, `npm test`, `npm run bench`, `npm run check:coverage` or `npm run check:settings-scope` fails.
2. Never publish without updating `CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Never run `npm version major` without explicit user confirmation that breaking changes are intended.
4. Always use `npm version <patch|minor|major> --no-git-tag-version`.
5. Never manually edit compiled output in `out/` or `out-test/`.
6. Never commit secrets or credentials (`VSCE_PAT`, `.env`, tokens, keys).
7. Always inspect package contents before publish with `vsce ls`, and confirm the package contains exactly one `out/extension.js` and no `src/`, `test/`, `.pmp/`, plan, spec or skill files.
8. Publishing is public and a version number can never be reused. Publish only after the user has explicitly told you to publish that specific version in the current conversation.
9. Never retry a failed publish in a loop, and never work around an authentication failure. Stop and report it.
10. If publish succeeded but a later step (commit, tag, push) failed, never publish again. Finish the remaining steps by hand.

## Build and Test Workflow

When asked to build, verify, or prepare a release:

1. Run `npm run compile`.
2. Run `npm test`.
3. Run `npm run bench`.
4. Run `npm run check:coverage` and `npm run check:settings-scope`.
5. Run `npm run build` to refresh the README build-status block.
6. Stop immediately and report failures if any command returns non-zero.

Expected success criteria:

- `out/extension.js` exists and matches `package.json.main`.
- All tests and benchmarks pass; checklist and settings-scope checks are green.
- README build-status block remains valid (auto-updated by build script).

## Changelog and Versioning Workflow

When asked to bump/release:

1. Write `CHANGELOG.md` entries under `## [Unreleased]` in user-facing language. Behavior changes that affect existing users (settings scope, data migration, files that are now refused) go in an `### Upgrading from X.x` subsection first, then `### Added`, `### Changed`, `### Fixed`. Verify each claim against the code before writing it.
2. Determine bump type from changes:
   - `patch`: fixes only
   - `minor`: backward-compatible features
   - `major`: breaking changes (needs explicit confirmation)
3. Run one command:
   - `npm version patch --no-git-tag-version`
   - `npm version minor --no-git-tag-version`
   - `npm version major --no-git-tag-version`
4. Move release notes from `Unreleased` into `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD`.
5. Recreate a fresh empty `## [Unreleased]` section at top.
6. Update the README release line: `Current release: vX.Y.Z`. Check that the README command list, privacy section and settings still match `package.json` (commands, settings, scopes).
7. Run `npm run build` again so status metadata is fresh after release edits.

Files that must stay in sync for a release:

- `package.json`
- `package-lock.json`
- `CHANGELOG.md`
- `README.md` (release line and build-status block)

## Publishing Workflow (Marketplace)

Run in this exact order:

1. Verify prereqs:
   - Working tree is clean apart from the release edits, and you know which branch you are on
   - Credentials: `VSCE_PAT` is set, or `npx @vscode/vsce ls-publishers` lists `aypande` (a listed publisher does not prove the token is still valid; an expired token only shows up at publish time)
   - `package.json` has correct `publisher`, `version`, `repository`, `license`, `icon`
   - `.vscodeignore` excludes source/tests/secrets from package
2. Run the full verification from "Build and Test Workflow".
3. Package:
   - `npm run package`
   - Artifact should be `plan-my-project-<version>.vsix` (gitignored)
4. Audit package contents:
   - `npx @vscode/vsce ls --no-yarn --no-dependencies`
   - Confirm exactly one `out/extension.js` (about 196 KB at 2.0.0, 28 files total). Many files under `out/` means a stray `tsc` emit polluted the bundle.
5. Get the explicit go-ahead for this version if not already given, then publish:
   - `npm run publish:vsce`
   - On "Personal Access Token ... expired" or any authentication error, stop. The user must create a new token (https://aka.ms/vscodepat) and run `npx @vscode/vsce login aypande`, or set `VSCE_PAT`. Do not retry.
6. Only after a successful publish, create VCS release metadata:
   - `git add package.json package-lock.json CHANGELOG.md README.md`
   - `git commit -m "chore: release vX.Y.Z"`
   - `git tag vX.Y.Z`
7. Push commit and tag after successful publish:
   - `git push origin <branch>`
   - `git push origin vX.Y.Z`
8. Record the release: mark the release unit done in `planmyproject.md` and add an entry to `FEATURE_PROGRESS.md`.

## Release Checklist

```text
[ ] CHANGELOG updated, behavior changes under "Upgrading from X.x"
[ ] Version bumped with --no-git-tag-version (major confirmed if breaking)
[ ] README "Current release", commands and privacy section match package.json
[ ] npm run compile, npm test, npm run bench pass
[ ] npm run check:coverage and npm run check:settings-scope pass
[ ] npm run build passes
[ ] VSIX packaged successfully
[ ] vsce ls reviewed: one out/extension.js, nothing unexpected
[ ] Credentials valid (publish does not fail on auth)
[ ] User explicitly approved publishing this version
[ ] Marketplace publish completed
[ ] release commit created
[ ] git tag vX.Y.Z created and pushed
[ ] planmyproject.md and FEATURE_PROGRESS.md updated
```

## Current Project Structure (Reference)

```text
PlanMyProject/
├── CHANGELOG.md  README.md  LICENSE  package.json  package-lock.json
├── esbuild.js                     # bundler: src/extension.ts -> out/extension.js
├── FEATURE_CHECKLIST.json         # feature -> test mapping, checked by check:coverage
├── FEATURE_PROGRESS.md            # progress log, including the v3 execution log
├── planmyproject.md               # this project's own plan (dogfooded)
├── .vscodeignore                  # keeps non-runtime files out of the VSIX
├── .github/workflows/ci.yml       # compile, test, bench, checklist, settings-scope
├── scripts/                       # update-readme-build-status, check-feature-coverage, check-settings-scope
├── skills/vscode-extension-publisher/   # release skill (also packaged as vscode-extension-publisher.skill)
├── src/                           # controller, model, parser, queue, scanner, ai, generation,
│                                  # research, debate, ui, storage, util + extension.ts
├── test/                          # *.test.ts, integration/, bench/, shims/vscode.js
├── media/  webviews/              # shipped assets
└── out/  out-test/                # build output (never edit by hand)
```

Keep this file aligned with `package.json` and release tooling whenever scripts or structure change.
